name: Revenue leaks on home-service websites: an audit of 290 sites (2026)
how_to_cite: Sami Enterprises, "Revenue leaks on home-service websites: an audit of 290 sites", 2026, samienterprises.co/research/. Data: samienterprises.co/research/290-site-audit.json.
method: Our 36-point revenue audit loads each site on a phone and a desktop, like a customer would. It never fills in or sends a form.
It checks 30 leak points, from the phone number to the estimate form, and 11 strengths.
A leak counts only when the check was at least 80% sure. Sites that didn't load were left out.
The sample is sites we chose to review, mostly Florida roofing, HVAC and plumbing companies. It is not a random sample of all businesses.
limits: The sample is not random. These are businesses we chose to contact, mostly in Florida.
The checker reads public pages only. It can miss a feature that sits behind a login, a pop-up or a page it did not open.
It can also flag a gap that a business covers some other way, like a phone team that answers every call.
A leak on a website is a sign of lost revenue, not a measured dollar loss.

findings.leak: No way to text or chat from the site
Estimate form with no photo upload, no timeline or budget question, or too many fields
No mention of a referral program
No promise of how fast you'll hear back
Phone number not on the first phone screen
No reviews shown on the site
Ad tracking installed, plus 2 or more gaps that can lose those visitors
